Carouge is one of the municipalities of the Canton of Geneva (Switzerland) covering a surface of 2.7 km2. The highest elevation is 386 m (1,266 ft), in June 2014 the population amounts to 21,125 inhabitants.

In 1754 Carouge was „invented“ by the duke of Savoy envisioning it as a trading competitor to Geneva, which was just 2 km away, on the other side of the river Arve. Due to religous tolerance the small hamlet quickly (18 years) grew to a prosperous town of fourthousand and became a refuge for Catholics and Jews and for Protestants tired of the puritan mentality ruling in Geneva.

These days I like to stroll through the criss-crossing streets and attractive buildings develloped by Turinese architects. Carouge is a refuge even nowadays, just in another way.

I am am entrepreneur. I work from home. Lucky me :-). I am very sociable and easy going person. Being growing up with a big family, I like people around me. I love to welcome people and get to know them. I have been hosting my family and friends in my guest room or my living room for quite a long time.

I am a passionate traveler. I try to travel frequently and have been all around the world (not in bottom of the world though..). Meet a stranger and become a friend it's a pleasure game for me. Airbnb giving us that opportunity.

I am looking forward to be your host.

Regards,

Anjo

Historic district of Geneva. According to Wikipedia: “Carouge has been part of the Republic and Canton of Geneva since 1816. It is famous for the “old Carouge” district, which retains a certain charm and where the terraces of the bistros are frequented when the sunny days return” But… Before 1816? Ho ho ho! According to the other tourist site, rts: “Nicknamed the Sardinian city, the territory was ceded to the Kingdom of Sardinia by the Republic of Geneva during the Treaty of Turin in 1754. Under the will of King Victor-Amadeus III of Sardinia, the hamlet is built in town by Piedmontese architects who give it its character. In 1786, the king granted it the title of Royal City. The commune has been united in Geneva since the Treaty of Turin of 1816." More detailed information also on the official Carouge website

Located in the Pâquis district, one of the liveliest and most cosmopolitan in Geneva, this flat is ideally situated, just a stone's throw from Lake Geneva. This dynamic district is renowned for its proximity to the lake, its many international restaurants, lively bars and public baths where locals love to relax in summer and winter alike.
Whether you're a lover of gastronomy, art or outdoor relaxation, you'll find it all nearby :
🌿 The Jardin Anglais and its famous Horloge Fleurie , an iconic spot perfect for a relaxing lakeside stroll
💦 Le Jet d'Eau , the unmissable symbol of Geneva, offering an impressive spectacle at any time of day
🛍 The shopping streets of the city centre , ideal for a shopping spree or a stroll through the luxury boutiques and local brands
🛶 Les Bains des Pâquis , a unique space where you can swim in the lake, enjoy the sauna or simply enjoy a fondue overlooking the water
